name: Adult orthodontics for looks

card.summary: Straightening teeth and correcting bite in adulthood with braces or clear aligners to improve the smile and lower face.
card.note: Teeth can drift back without retainers; adults may have periodontal and bone factors to plan around.

quick.overview:
Adult orthodontics moves teeth into better alignment using braces, lingual braces or clear aligners after growth has finished. People pursue it to fix crowding, gaps, overbite or crossbite, which changes the smile and how the lower face and profile look.

Reviews describe adults as motivated, cooperative patients, with the caveat that adult expectations can be high and need to be discussed at the start. Treatment typically takes one to two years, and jaw surgery is an option for severe skeletal cases when growth is complete.
quick.how: Treatment begins with an orthodontist's assessment, then braces (metal, ceramic or on the tongue side) or removable clear aligners worn for the prescribed hours. Appointments are spread every four to ten weeks for braces, and retainers follow treatment. One forum user planning treatment asked about aligner brands and budgeted several thousand dollars.
quick.risks: Reported issues include decalcification and decay with poor hygiene, root resorption, gum and periodontal considerations in adults, and relapse; over half of patients show some tooth movement back within ten years, which is why retainers are used. Jaw surgery carries surgical risks.

lead: Adult orthodontics is orthodontic treatment carried out after growth has finished, using fixed braces, lingual braces or clear aligners to straighten teeth and correct bite problems.[1][2] Adults seek it for appearance, function or as preparation for restorative work.[3][4]

For looks, aligned teeth and a corrected overbite or crossbite change the smile and can alter the facial profile; a looksmax.org user in his twenties described a minor overbite and crossbite visible in side profile and a mouth that moved to one side when speaking, and asked about aligner options on a budget of five to eight thousand dollars.[5]
Literature on adult patients describes them as highly motivated but with expectations that must be managed.[1][6]

chain: Smile and lower-face profile look more balanced
angle.text: Moving the teeth changes visible alignment and bite, which changes the smile and can change profile appearance. Severe skeletal discrepancies may involve jaw surgery rather than tooth movement alone.

infobox: Metal, ceramic or lingual braces; clear aligners

paras: Adult cases differ from adolescent ones because bones adjust less readily and gum and periodontal health, missing teeth, existing crowns and temporomandibular issues need planning.[1][3][6] Appliances include metal and ceramic braces, lingual braces and clear aligners; a consensus statement from the Angle Society of Europe addresses aligner treatment.[7][8] Bonding brackets to porcelain restorations is a recognized technical issue in adults.[9]

Wikipedia notes braces usually last one to three years and retainers are worn long term because over 50 percent of patients show some relapse within ten years.[10] If skeletal growth is complete, jaw surgery is an option for severe cases.[10] Review articles discuss clear aligners' stability and success, accelerated tooth movement using surgical techniques and age-related alveolar bone changes.[11][12][13]
Surveys and reviews examine what adult patients want, how they comply, and the relationship between treatment and satisfaction.[14][15] A review of 1995 noted adult demand was rising.[1]

On looksmax.org, an adult user asked about low-cost aligners for overbite and crossbite and whether removing wisdom teeth would improve symmetry; one reply reported noticing no change five months after their own removal.[5]

Controlled studies in adults include a randomized trial of alternating maxillary expansion and constriction in young adults and registered trials of piezoelectric corticotomy to speed tooth movement.[16][17][18] A registered study assesses psychological factors in adults seeking treatment.[19]

timeline.event: Lawrence Andrews introduces the straight-wire appliance.[10]

lore.intro: Forum discussion focuses on cost, aligner brands and effects on symmetry.[5]

claims.claim: Removing wisdom teeth can improve facial symmetry
claims.believers: A user planning removal asked whether it would help symmetry.[5]
claims.experts: No study in the cited material tests this; one replying user reported no change.[5]
